holding_summary: The court held that occupancy of the dwelling unit by three rent-paying roomers or boarders exceeded the two-boarder limit of the Multiple Dwelling Law and Code, and that this illegal occupancy, combined with a nonconforming door/transom at the room's egress, established the landlord's prima facie case for possession. It was therefore error for the trial court to have dismissed the landlord's summary proceeding.

quotes.text: The testimony in behalf of the landlord, without contradiction by tenant, established the premises were used and occupied by three rent-paying roomers or boarders. This constituted a single-room occupancy in violation of the Multiple Dwelling Law (§ 3, subd. 4) and the Multiple Dwelling Code of the City of New York (Administrative Code of City of New York, § D26-3.7) which limits the number of permissible boarders, roomers or lodgers to two.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
holding_summary: New York rent regulation decontrols a one- or two-family dwelling unit where an owner lets nonhousekeeping furnished space to no more than two paying tenants while occupying the remainder of the unit, but this exemption is forfeited once the letting becomes a housekeeping arrangement rather than single-family occupancy. Because the landlord here rented part of the unit for housekeeping purposes, the exemption terminated and control was restored.

quotes.text: They also remain decontrolled and not subject to rent control where the letting is of nonhousekeeping, furnished housing accommodation, located within a single-dwelling unit not used as a rooming or boarding house, provided not more than two tenants pay rent and live in such dwelling unit, and the remaining portion of such dwelling unit is occupied by the landlord or his immediate family.

The landlord respondent having rented part of the dwelling unit for housekeeping purposes, the housing accommodation was occupied for other than single-family occupancy and the exemption from control terminated.
The final order should be reversed, with $30 costs, and final order awarded the tenant dismissing the petition on the merits, with costs.

notes: General rule recognizing owner letting of up to two paying lodgers while occupying the remainder is favorable framework; specific application here found the exemption forfeited, hence mixed polarity.
